study type: cross-sectional study nested within prospective cohorts
exposure: dissatisfaction with the care received during childbirth
cohort: The study included 2160 women 12 to 24 months postpartum from two Brazilian cities.
finding: The incidence of chronic pelvic pain was 12.7%, and C-sections doubled the odds of developing chronic pelvic pain.
mod_finding: C-sections doubled the odds of developing chronic pelvic pain and were associated with a 6.1% higher incidence of CPP compared to those who did not undergo the procedure.
